description: South Dakota-only rules checked against the Codified Laws, administrative rule 61:18:02, and the Department of Public Safety. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Except as provided under section 32-25-7, the maximum speed on South Dakota's interstate highways is
questions.explanation: SDCL 32-25-4 says that except as provided pursuant to section 32-25-7, no person may drive on the national system of interstate highways at a speed in excess of eighty miles per hour.

questions.q: Except for the interstate rule in section 32-25-4 and speeds set under section 32-25-7, South Dakota's maximum speed is
questions.explanation: SDCL 32-25-1.1 says that except as provided by section 32-25-4 or pursuant to section 32-25-7, no person may drive on a street or highway at a speed in excess of sixty-five miles per hour.

questions.q: In a South Dakota urban area that is not zoned or posted under section 32-25-7, the maximum lawful speed is
questions.explanation: SDCL 32-25-12 says that in urban areas which are not zoned or posted as provided in section 32-25-7, the maximum lawful speed shall be twenty-five miles per hour.

questions.q: When passing a South Dakota school during a recess, or while children are going to or leaving school during opening or closing hours, the maximum lawful speed is
questions.explanation: SDCL 32-25-14 sets fifteen miles per hour when passing a school during a school recess or while children are going to or leaving school during the opening or closing hours.

questions.q: A 70 mph limit on a divided four-lane rural South Dakota state trunk highway applies when
options: Every divided highway uses 70 with or without signs
The Commission sets it by rule and signs are posted
The road is inside a city
The interstate 80 mph limit has been repealed
questions.explanation: SDCL 32-25-7.1 says the Transportation Commission may establish, by rules, a maximum of seventy miles per hour on any divided four-lane highway in a rural area on the state trunk system. The Department of Transportation shall conspicuously post signs at the beginning and end of that portion.

questions.q: South Dakota prohibits driving or being in actual physical control of a vehicle when chemical analysis shows alcohol of
options: 0.02 percent or more for every driver
questions.explanation: SDCL 32-23-1(1) prohibits driving or actual physical control while there is 0.08 percent or more by weight of alcohol in the person's blood as shown by chemical analysis of breath, blood, or other bodily substance.

questions.q: It is a Class 2 misdemeanor for a South Dakota driver under 21 to drive when there is physical evidence of alcohol of
questions.explanation: SDCL 32-23-21(1) makes it a Class 2 misdemeanor for any person under 21 to drive, operate, or be in actual physical control if there is physical evidence of 0.02 percent or more by weight of alcohol as shown by chemical analysis of breath, blood, or other bodily substance.

questions.q: South Dakota prohibits driving a commercial motor vehicle while the alcohol concentration is
questions.explanation: SDCL 32-12A-44 says no person may drive or be in actual physical control of a commercial motor vehicle while there is between 0.04 and 0.08 percent or more, by weight, of alcohol in that person's blood as shown by chemical analysis of breath, blood, or other body substance.

questions.q: A South Dakota operator is subject to license or privilege suspension after accumulating
questions.explanation: SDCL 32-12-49.2 says an operator is subject to suspension who, under the schedule in section 32-12-49.1, has been convicted of traffic violations resulting in 15 points within any 12 consecutive months or 22 points within any 24 consecutive months.

questions.q: The first South Dakota suspension for reaching the point totals in section 32-12-49.2 is
questions.explanation: Administrative rule 61:18:02:10 says that if the record shows 15 points in any 12 consecutive months or 22 points in any 24 consecutive months, the department shall suspend for 60 days on the first suspension, six months on the second, and one year on the third or subsequent suspension.

questions.q: On the South Dakota point table published by the Department of Public Safety, reckless driving is
questions.explanation: The Department of Public Safety point table lists reckless driving as 8 points, eluding and drag racing as 6, failure to yield, improper passing, and driving on the wrong side as 4, a stop sign or light violation as 3, and other moving violations as 2. Driving under the influence is listed as 10 points, with a note that state law requires revocation for that offense.

questions.q: The minimum age for a South Dakota instruction permit is
questions.explanation: SDCL 32-12-11: a person at least fourteen but less than eighteen years of age who holds no license or permit applies to the Department of Public Safety for an instruction permit.

questions.q: For a South Dakota instruction permit issued on or after July 1, 2020, the holding period before a restricted minor's permit is
options: 30 days with or without driver education
Six months only if the driver is already 16
questions.explanation: SDCL 32-12-12: with an approved driver-education course, the instruction permit must be held one hundred eighty continuous days if issued on or after July 1, 2020. Without it, SDCL 32-12-11 requires at least two hundred seventy-five days for a permit issued after July 1, 2020.

questions.q: Unless the instruction permit was issued before July 1, 2020, moving to a South Dakota restricted minor's permit requires supervised driving of
options: 50 hours: 10 at night, 10 in bad weather
No logged hours if the driver is 14
questions.explanation: SDCL 32-12-11: a minor holding an instruction permit issued after July 1, 2020, shall drive at least fifty hours under the supervision of a parent, legal guardian, or licensed driver over eighteen with at least one year of driving experience. Ten of those hours must be in inclement weather and at least ten at night.

questions.q: For the first 6 months of a South Dakota restricted minor's permit, passengers are limited to
options: Only immediate family or household members
Any passenger if the trip is in daylight
questions.explanation: Section 32-12-12.5 says a holder of a restricted minor's permit may not carry any passenger other than a member of the driver's immediate family or household during the first six months. After that, the holder is limited to no more than one passenger under 18 who is not an immediate family member or a person whose primary residence is the same household. The limit does not apply when the holder is accompanied by a parent or guardian, or by a passenger who is at least 18, has one year of driving experience, and lives in the same household.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in South Dakota complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: South Dakota requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.
questions.remember: South Dakota: 50 hours of supervised driving.

questions.q: Of a South Dakota teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: South Dakota requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: South Dakota: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

questions.q: In South Dakota, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 14½ years.
questions.remember: South Dakota: driving alone from 14½ years.

provenance.manual: Driver Licensing Information for Teen Drivers and Parents - SD.gov

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in South Dakota not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: South Dakota restricts provisional drivers from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: South Dakota new drivers: off the road 10 p.m. to 6 a.m..

questions.q: In South Dakota, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: South Dakota drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 16 years.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the South Dakota car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the South Dakota car knowledge test.
questions.remember: South Dakota car test: pass with 80%.

provenance.manual: Driver Licensing Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) - SD.gov

questions.q: In South Dakota, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: South Dakota, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

questions.q: In South Dakota, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in South Dakota brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: South Dakota, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a South Dakota residential district?
questions.explanation: South Dakota sets 25 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in South Dakota?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in South Dakota can be posted up to 80 mph for cars.
questions.remember: South Dakota rural interstate: up to 80 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes South Dakota's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: South Dakota: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.
questions.remember: South Dakota phone law: hands-free only.

questions.q: How is South Dakota's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: South Dakota seat belt enforcement is secondary.
questions.remember: South Dakota seat belts: secondary law.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in South Dakota?
questions.explanation: South Dakota requires a car seat or booster until 5 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: South Dakota: car or booster seat until 5 years.

questions.q: What is South Dakota's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: South Dakota requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.
